title: Sort down on bathing-suits and lownecks of course nobody wanted her to wear
html_source: In this line, and some lines that follow, it is clear that we are in Molly Bloom’s mind, and that we are hearing her more mean thoughts directed towards Mrs. Riordan. She insults Mrs. Riordan’s appearance because she is spiteful of her not giving the Bloom family money. Rather than calling her cheap, she calls her ugly. This show that Molly Bloom can be seen more as a shallow character.
